transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Marin (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Opal CTO), Priya Rao (Platform Eng), Marcus Li (Eng Manager)

Auto Summary: quick chat to figure out time-to-first-token using Redwood API free credits, plus questions on dedicated vs private for compliance. Customer wants to run a 1-week pilot and a small benchmark. Security (SAML, KMS), data residency discussed. Action items at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira Khan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we said 30 minutes but we have about 40 so we can go a bit deeper. quick intro from our side real fast. i'm samira i'm the account lead for redwood inference.
[00:10] Diego Marin: and i'm diego, solutions eng. i'll try not to be too nerdy but i'll answer infra and perf stuff.
[00:18] Alex Chen: alex here, cto at opal systems. thanks for squeezing us in, we've been poking around your hosted api and the docs, curious about the 'time to first token' path and what minimal friction looks like.
[00:30] Priya Rao: hey everyone, priya, platform eng. i'm mostly worried about security and data flow. we have strict logs retention and KMS for keys.
[00:38] Marcus Li: marcus, engineering manager, linting in on the integration portion and overall cost.
[00:45] Diego Marin: great, totally. so maybe quick agenda: free credits/redwood plg flow, the SDK quickstart, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and then we can talk about a very small pilot, right?
[00:55] Alex Chen: perfect. can you start with the free credits and how long they last? that's the first gating piece for our PM.
[01:04] Samira Khan: yeah, so for plg quickstarts we give a credits bundle that covers about 50k tokens of generation or equivalent, um it's a soft bundle for 30 days from signup. you can also request an extension for pilots, we usually do that for enterprise prospects.
[01:18] Alex Chen: 30 days, okay. 50k tokens roughly how many API calls for chat? we're doing short prompts, like 200 tokens in, 100 tokens out.
[01:27] Diego Marin: that math works out to ~166 calls. but for evals we often advise batching where possible. also you can switch to embeddings which will cost differently. but for your use case, the credits should be enough for an initial sprint.
[01:40] Priya Rao: quick Q on credits redemption, is it self-serve on the console or do you provision it for us?
[01:46] Samira Khan: self-serve redemption in the console, there's also a code we can email that auto-applies; i'll send that. note for private deployments credits don't apply, that's covered in licensing.
[01:58] Marcus Li: when you say private deployments, you mean vpc/on-prem? what's the minimal setup time, like days/weeks?
[02:06] Diego Marin: good question. hosted api gets you to first request in minutes; dedicated might take a few days for provisioning and capacity mapping; private (VPC or on-prem) is more involved — generally 2-6 weeks depending on network approvals and if you need HSM/KMS integrations.
[02:25] Alex Chen: that's helpful. for us compliance is a major factor. we need SAML SSO, audit logs, and bring-your-own-key to KMS. does redwood support those out of the box for hosted?
[02:35] Diego Marin: hosted supports SAML SSO (via SSO provider), audit logs at request (we can enable log streaming), and BYOK is available via KMS integrations for private and dedicated customers; hosted has encryption at rest but full customer-managed keys are typically an enterprise feature tied to Dedicated or Private.
[02:52] Priya Rao: hm, we might need BYOK. can you share the security whitepaper and SOC2 evidence as part of the next steps?
[02:59] Samira Khan: absolutely, i'll include SOC 2, iso summary, and our security whitepaper. also we'll include an architecture note on how BYOK works across our modes.
[03:09] Marcus Li: you mentioned 'time-to-first-token' minutes for hosted. can you run through the quickstart flow? like code examples, SDKs, and typical dev steps.
[03:18] Diego Marin: sure — minimal flow: sign up, redeem credits, create api key in console, then one curl call or use our js/python sdk. example: POST to /v1/generate with model param. latency-wise for small chat calls we usually see 50-150ms token streaming on the hosted clusters for the base models. but that varies.
[03:36] Alex Chen: is that 50-150ms per token or total response latency?
[03:40] Diego Marin: we mean per-token streaming latency. end-to-end user-perceived latency depends on prompt length and output length; short single-shot prompts can be in the low hundreds ms.
[03:49] Alex Chen: okay, that's promising. can you do a controlled benchmark with our prompt set? we care about p95 latency.
[03:55] Diego Marin: yes, we can propose a micro-benchmark plan: we run hosted calls against the model variant you pick, measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens, and then compare a dedicated config. it's usually a day for a small run.
[04:08] Priya Rao: cost per 1k tokens, are you able to share rough numbers now? ballpark.
[04:12] Samira Khan: ballpark for hosted depends on model; for curated open models it's approx $0.5 - $1.5 per 1k tokens for generation tiers, but we'll send a tailored estimate. for dedicated the unit cost drops but you have fixed monthly commit.
[04:28] Marcus Li: that pricing delta is the tricky bit for us. we need to justify dedicated if we commit.
[04:33] Diego Marin: yeah it's the usual tradeoff: dedicated = predictable throughput, lower marginal unit cost, and isolation. hosted = fastest time to value and lower ops burden.
[04:42] Alex Chen: we also have an internal requirement for data residency in eu-west. do you have hosted regions in europe?
[04:48] Diego Marin: we do, euro-west and london regions are available; we can pin requests to region via a routing header or per API key setting.
[04:57] Priya Rao: for pilot data, can we redact PII client-side and still use the platform? or do you need special onboarding for redaction?
[05:03] Diego Marin: you can do client-side redaction, we also offer built-in redaction hooks in the SDK for common patterns. for any sensitive production pipeline we typically recommend private/dedicated with BYOK.
[05:13] Alex Chen: ok. i wanted to surface something: our legal team will want to know about data retention and whether logs include full prompts. how is that handled?
[05:21] Samira Khan: default hosted logs retain request metadata and a hashed prompt fingerprint for diagnostics; full prompt storage is configurable — for enterprise customers we can turn off request retention and enable streaming of logs to customer S3 if desired.
[05:32] Marcus Li: is that part of the onboarding checklist? who owns that config?
[05:35] Diego Marin: onboarding handles it; se sets up tenant config with your security contact, and the CSM coordinates retention policies. we'll document all options.
[05:44] Alex Chen: good. two more quick things: SDK language coverage and community support? our frontend is react/node.
[05:51] Diego Marin: we have first-class JS and Python sdks, unofficial community sdks for go/ruby but you can always use raw REST. community slack and github examples plenty.
[05:59] Priya Rao: can you show a minimal curl example? i'll paste it later in the message thread.
[06:04] Diego Marin: sure, here's the gist — curl POST with api key in header, body with prompt array and model id. i'll paste the exact snippet in the follow-up email.
[06:12] Alex Chen: thanks. about the pilot scope, we're thinking a week-long eval that runs a 1k-sample prompt set across a few models to measure latencies and cost. is that doable within credits or will we need to top up?
[06:23] Samira Khan: depends on token counts; if each sample is ~300 tokens total, 1k samples is 300k tokens, which exceeds the free credits. we can either expand the credit grant for the pilot or run a smaller focused set. typical approach: we give an extended pilot credit + a small dedicated benchmark budget.
[06:41] Marcus Li: extending credits sounds fair. what about provisioning a dedicated short-lived instance for the pilot? like a week of dedicated capacity?
[06:48] Diego Marin: technically possible but provisioning dedicated for a week is uncommon because it needs capacity mapping; however we can do a canary dedicated test in shared infra or simulate dedicated by reserving capacity on our staging cluster — it's doable but we'd propose hosted benchmark first.
[07:02] Alex Chen: okay, hosted bench first makes sense.
[07:06] Priya Rao: last sec question: SSO integration timelines, we use Okta — how long to get that in place?
[07:11] Diego Marin: Okta SAML can be configured within a day once you provide metadata; full end-to-end SSO testing might take 2-3 days with your IDP team.
[07:20] Samira Khan: to summarize next steps: i'll send credits and quickstart, diego will send benchmark plan and code snippets, and we'll schedule a security deep dive with our security engineer. customer will send redacted sample prompt set and compliance checklist.
[07:35] Alex Chen: sounds good — can we aim to start the pilot week of 2026-08-24? that's our sprint cadence.
[07:42] Samira Khan: yes we can aim for that. i'll block tentative follow-up for 2026-08-25 and invite security.
[07:51] Marcus Li: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:53] Speaker 3: (inaudible) thanks bye.

End of transcript.
